$comment: The models catalog that renders the Models section. One file: lab × model × way-in × subscription × seat line, shaped to be replaced by TeamCLI's own registry (registry/models.json) without changing the pages. The five ways in are the matrix columns; each transport names the way it is. Every route is marked verified (a seat we have run) or listed (a documented route not yet run). Nothing here is a price or a benchmark; sign-up and pricing live on each vendor's own pages, linked. Seat lines use the reference team-file seats schema, which requires cli, vendor, model, version and launch; a seat whose launcher picks the model sets model_from: launcher. Verified by the team on the catalog's own date.

Jules picks its own Gemini model, and the jules binary answers no --version.

families.name: Claude Opus
families.tagline: Anthropic's line for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work.
families.summary: Claude Opus is Anthropic's line for work that runs long and thinks hard: multi-step coding agents, changes across a whole repository, and knowledge work that wants the full context window. Opus 5.5, the current version, sits below Fable and above Sonnet in Anthropic's lineup, at a quarter of Fable's price.
good: Long multi-step coding runs — Terminal-Bench 4.0 agentic coding at 66.4% (vendor-reported)
Knowledge work with tools — Humanity's Last Exam 67.7% with tools (vendor-reported)
Computer use — OSWorld 2.1 at 81.8% (vendor-reported)
limits: Not the cheapest per token — Sonnet 5.5 is half the price, Haiku 5.5 a fraction of it
Below Fable on the hardest long-horizon work; Anthropic positions Fable for when Opus at higher effort falls short

families.name: Claude Sonnet
families.tagline: The Claude line that balances speed and intelligence.
families.summary: Claude Sonnet is the middle of Anthropic's lineup, and on Anthropic's own Terminal-Bench 4.0 table its top scorer for agentic coding. Sonnet 5.5 turns in outputs more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5 while keeping the 1M-token context window, at half Opus 5.5's price.
good: Agentic coding at speed — Terminal-Bench 4.0 70.6%, the top of Anthropic's own table (vendor-reported)
Fast for its class — outputs 30%+ faster than Sonnet 5 (vendor-reported)
Half Opus 5.5's price at $2 in / $10 out per MTok
limits: Below Opus and Fable on the most demanding long-horizon work
FrontierCode 1.1 trails Opus 5.5 — 46.2% at max effort against 54.4% (vendor-reported)

families.name: Claude Haiku
families.tagline: The fast, cheap Claude — for sub-agents, quick checks and high-volume steps.
families.summary: Claude Haiku is the smallest of the Claude lineup, and a great little fighter: fast at standard speed, a tenth of Sonnet's input price, and — on Haiku 5.5 — a Terminal-Bench 4.0 score no previous Haiku came near. Anthropic's own positioning is high-volume, latency-sensitive work: classification, routing, extraction, subagent tasks.
good: Sub-agents and quick checks — the work where waiting costs more than thinking
High-volume steps at $0.10 in / $0.50 out per MTok for prompts up to 100k tokens
Anthropic's fastest model to date at standard speed (vendor-reported)
limits: Not the model for the hardest agentic coding — Terminal-Bench 4.0 39.2% against Sonnet 5.5's 70.6% (vendor-reported)
Prompts over 100,000 tokens step up to $0.50 in / $2.50 out per MTok
reach: Claude Code lists Claude Haiku on its own model screen, so a seat with model: Claude Haiku runs it the same way the Opus and Sonnet seats run theirs.
Cursor and Antigravity list it among the Claude models on their plans.

families.name: Claude Fable
families.tagline: Anthropic's deepest reasoner — for work where Opus at higher effort falls short.
families.summary: Claude Fable is the top of Anthropic's lineup: always-on thinking, the longest horizon, the highest price. Anthropic's own guidance is to reach for Fable when Opus at a higher effort setting falls short. It shares the rest of the lineup's shape — the 1M-token context and 128K output window.
good: The hardest long-horizon agentic work; Anthropic's pick when Opus at higher effort falls short
FrontierCode v1.1 at 50.3% — above Opus 5's 48.0% on Anthropic's own table (vendor-reported)
limits: The most expensive Claude at $10 in / $50 out per MTok
Slower than the rest of the lineup (Anthropic's own comparative)

families.name: Claude Mythos
families.tagline: Fable's capabilities for verified organizations, behind Anthropic's verification program.
families.summary: Claude Mythos is Fable's twin: the same capabilities, context window and pricing, offered only to organizations that pass Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program. It exists so high-assurance organizations can run the top of the lineup under their own clearance; everyone else uses Fable.
good: Fable 5.1's specifications and pricing under an organizational verification gate
limits: Limited availability — Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program, not a self-serve model
No TeamCLI route: Claude Code's model screen lists Opus, Sonnet, Haiku and Fable only

families.name: Gemini Argon
families.tagline: Google's flagship reasoning line — a 1M-token unified context, outputs up to 1M.
families.summary: Gemini Argon is the top of Google's lineup: reasoning-first, a million-token unified context, and a long-decode mode that answers with up to a million tokens. Its introductory pricing runs through November 30, 2026, then doubles.
good: Very large inputs and very long outputs — long decode answers with up to 1M tokens
Flagship reasoning with thinking effort adjustable from low to high
limits: No benchmarks published by Google — no coding-agent figures to cite
The price doubles on December 1, 2026, to $4 in / $20 out per MTok

families.name: Gemini Pro
families.tagline: Google's general-purpose tier between Argon and Flash.
families.summary: Gemini Pro is the balanced line of the Gemini family. The current 3.1 Pro is a preview with tiered pricing; 2.5 Pro remains available with access limited. Google publishes no benchmarks for the line, and no TeamCLI seat runs it.
good: The middle tier — heavier than Flash, lighter than Argon
limits: 3.1 Pro is in preview and 2.5 Pro is access-limited
No benchmarks published by Google

families.name: Gemini Flash
families.tagline: Google's fast line for long-horizon software engineering and autonomous agents.
families.summary: Gemini Flash is Google's fast tier — in Google's own words for 3.8 Flash, engineered for long-horizon software engineering and autonomous agents. It undercuts Argon at $0.75 in / $3.75 out per MTok on introductory pricing, and four versions are offered today.
good: Agentic coding loops where the cost per iteration matters
Four versions offered, from 3.8 Flash down to the access-limited 2.5
limits: Introductory pricing doubles on January 1, 2027
No benchmarks published by Google

families.name: Gemini Flash-Lite
families.tagline: Google's fastest, cheapest tier — the one for high-volume steps.
families.summary: Flash-Lite is the floor of the Gemini lineup: the fastest, most cost-effective tier in Google's own description. For coding agents it is the model for high-volume steps — sweeps, triage, sub-agent checks — at $0.30 in / $2.50 out per MTok.
good: The cheapest Gemini text tier for high-volume steps
limits: The lightest model of the lineup; Google publishes no benchmarks for it

families.name: GPT Astra
families.tagline: OpenAI's most capable line, for the most demanding work.
families.summary: GPT-6 Astra is the top of OpenAI's lineup — the most capable model for the most demanding work, in OpenAI's own words. It carries a 1.05M-token context (922K max input), a 128K output window, and the highest price in the catalog at $10 in / $50 out per MTok.
good: The most demanding work, with the deepest context at 1.05M tokens
limits: The most expensive OpenAI line; prompts over 272k tokens double the input price
No benchmarks published by OpenAI

families.name: GPT Sol
families.tagline: OpenAI's near-flagship line for complex work at a lower cost.
families.summary: GPT Sol is OpenAI's workhorse line for complex work: near-Astra performance at a fifth of the price, in OpenAI's own positioning. GPT-6.1 Sol is the current version, and the one TeamCLI has run — verified through Codex, listed through Antigravity and Cursor.
good: Complex coding work at $2 in / $10 out per MTok
Three ways in — verified through Codex, listed through Antigravity and Cursor
limits: No benchmarks published by OpenAI
The 5.6 promotional price ($4/$20) runs at least through November 21, 2026

families.name: GPT Terra
families.tagline: OpenAI's mid-tier line, priced between Sol and Astra on output.
families.summary: GPT Terra is OpenAI's middle line: $2 in / $12 out per MTok, between Sol and Astra on output price. OpenAI's pages carry no positioning for it beyond the price and the long-context tiers.
good: A mid tier at $2 in / $12 out per MTok when a step needs more than Sol
limits: No benchmarks published by OpenAI, and no positioning on its own model pages

families.name: GPT Luna
families.tagline: OpenAI's focused, high-volume tier — the cheap, fast one.
families.summary: GPT-6 Luna is OpenAI's cheap tier — for focused, high-volume tasks in OpenAI's own words — at $0.10 in / $0.50 out per MTok, a twentieth of Sol's input price. It shares the 1.05M-token context with the rest of the current line.
good: High-volume steps at $0.10 in / $0.50 out per MTok
The same 1.05M-token context as Sol and Astra
limits: A focused tier, not a frontier one; no benchmarks published by OpenAI

families.name: GPT Codex
families.tagline: OpenAI's line built for coding, named for the Codex CLI.
families.summary: GPT-5.3 Codex is OpenAI's coding-specialized model, priced below Sol at $1.75 in / $14 out per MTok, with a Fast tier at $3.50/$28 that trades price for speed. TeamCLI's Codex seats run the Sol line today.
good: Coding-specialized, at $1.75 in / $14 out per MTok
A priced Fast tier — $3.50/$28 — for steps that need the faster variant
limits: No benchmarks published by OpenAI; no TeamCLI seat has run it yet
reach: Run by the Codex CLI — the same codex transport as the Sol seats, pointed at gpt-5.3-codex.

families.name: GPT Cyber
families.tagline: OpenAI's line for authorized vulnerability research and security testing.
families.summary: GPT-5.6 Cyber (Daybreak) is OpenAI's security-research line, gated to authorized vulnerability research and security testing. At $12.50 in / $75 out per MTok it is the most expensive model in OpenAI's catalog, above Astra.
good: Authorized security testing and vulnerability research — its purpose
limits: Gated to authorized use, per OpenAI's terms
No TeamCLI route, and no benchmarks published by OpenAI

families.name: GPT Rosalind
families.tagline: OpenAI's life-sciences line, for approved organizations.
families.summary: GPT-Rosalind is OpenAI's line for life-sciences research, offered as Research and Discovery variants at $5 in / $25 out per MTok to approved organizations, with billing from October 5, 2026. It is not a general coding model.
good: Life-sciences research work, for approved organizations
limits: Approved organizations only; not a coding-agent line
No TeamCLI route, and no benchmarks published by OpenAI

families.name: Grok
families.tagline: xAI's flagship line — its most capable model, recommended for code and chat.
families.summary: Grok is xAI's main line. Grok 4.7 is xAI's most capable model and its recommendation for coding; the 4.3 tier trades capability for a million-token context at $1.25 in / $2.50 out per MTok. TeamCLI runs 4.7 both by the Grok CLI and through Cursor.
good: Coding and chat — xAI's own recommendation for Grok 4.7
500K-token context at $2 in / $6 out per MTok for prompts under 200k tokens
The 4.3 tier: 1M-token context at $1.25 in / $2.50 out per MTok
limits: No benchmarks published by xAI, and no release dates on its model pages
Prompts of 200k tokens and up step up to $4 in / $12 out per MTok

families.name: Grok Build
families.tagline: xAI's coding-focused model, priced under the main line.
families.summary: Grok Build 0.1 is xAI's coding-specialized model: a 256K-token context at $1 in / $2 out per MTok — the cheapest way into a Grok model. xAI publishes no dates or benchmarks for it.
good: Coding work at $1 in / $2 out per MTok with a 256K-token context
limits: No benchmarks and no release date published
No TeamCLI route yet — the Grok CLI seats run the main Grok line

families.name: DeepSeek Flash
families.tagline: DeepSeek's fast line — vision, a 1M context, and prices at cents.
families.summary: DeepSeek Flash is the fast line of DeepSeek's pair: vision supported, thinking on by default, a 1M-token context and a 384K output window. Off-peak input (cache miss) is $0.15 per MTok, peak $0.30; output $0.60 off-peak, $1.20 peak.
good: Agentic coding at cents per MTok
Vision input and a 384K output window
Off-peak hours halve the price — weekdays outside 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC
limits: No benchmarks published by DeepSeek
Peak-hour pricing doubles; the headline prices are cache-miss input

families.name: DeepSeek Pro
families.tagline: DeepSeek's larger line — no vision, triple Flash's output price.
families.summary: DeepSeek V4 Pro is the heavier of DeepSeek's pair: the same 1M-token context and 384K output window, no vision input, and roughly triple Flash's price — $1.98 out off-peak, $3.96 peak.
good: The heavier DeepSeek line, for work past Flash's ceiling
limits: No vision input, and no benchmarks published by DeepSeek
Triple Flash's price on output
reach: The same Claude Code endpoint route as the Flash seat, pointed at deepseek-v4-pro; no seat has run it yet.

families.name: Kimi K3
families.tagline: Moonshot's flagship — long-horizon coding and knowledge work, 2.8T parameters.
families.summary: Kimi K3 is Moonshot's flagship: 2.8 trillion parameters, native vision, a 1M-token context, effort up to max. Moonshot positions it for long-horizon coding and knowledge work. TeamCLI runs it today as a Claude Code endpoint seat; the native Kimi CLI is listed but has no launch profile yet.
good: Long-horizon coding and knowledge work — Moonshot's own positioning
Native vision with a 1M-token context
Cached input at $0.30 per MTok — a tenth of fresh input
limits: No benchmarks published by Moonshot
No native-CLI launch profile yet — the endpoint route is the way in today

families.name: Kimi K2
families.tagline: Moonshot's coding-specialist line, with a priced highspeed variant.
families.summary: Kimi K2 is Moonshot's coding line: K2.7 Code at a 256K context ($0.95 in / $4 out per MTok), a highspeed variant at about 180 tokens per second of output ($1.90/$8), and K2.6 for general work. The one vendor-published output speed in this catalog belongs here.
good: Dedicated coding at $0.95 in / $4 out per MTok
The highspeed variant: about 180 tokens/s of output, up to 260 in short context (vendor-published)
Cache hits at $0.19 per MTok
limits: A 256K context — a quarter of K3's
No benchmarks published by Moonshot
reach: The same Claude Code endpoint route that runs K3 would run the K2 line; no seat has run it yet.

families.name: GLM
families.tagline: Z.ai's frontier line — reasoning always on, a 1M context.
families.summary: GLM is Z.ai's main line. GLM-5.3 turns reasoning on always (effort low to max, max by default), reads a 1M-token context, and made its largest coding jump in the family's history over GLM-5.2, on Z.ai's own benchmarks. Older versions stay served at lower prices.
good: Agentic coding — Terminal-Bench 3.0 28.3 against GLM-5.2's 4.6, DeepSWE v1.1 66.9 against 46.2 (vendor-reported)
Reasoning always on with adjustable effort; a 1M context at $1.40 in / $4.40 out per MTok
Older versions still served at lower prices (GLM-5, then 4.7/4.6/4.5)
limits: Text-only input — no vision
The benchmarks are Z.ai's own, measured its way; no independent figures may be republished here

families.name: GLM Flash
families.tagline: Z.ai's cheap, fast companion line.
families.summary: GLM Flash is Z.ai's fast tier: GLM-5.3 Flash at $0.15 in / $0.50 out per MTok with cache reads at $0.03, and FlashX, the faster variant, at $0.37/$1.25. The 4.x Flash models are free.
good: High-volume steps at $0.15 in / $0.50 out per MTok
Free 4.x Flash models for try-out work
limits: No benchmarks published by Z.ai for the Flash line
No TeamCLI seat has run it — the endpoint seats run the main GLM line
reach: The same Claude Code endpoint route as the GLM 5.3 seat, pointed at glm-5.3-flash; no seat has run it yet.

families.name: Muse Wonder
families.tagline: Meta's frontier coding line — long-running agents and computer use.
families.summary: Muse Wonder is the top of Meta's Muse lineup: frontier coding, long-running agents, advanced computer use. Meta says Wonder Full tops agentic and coding benchmarks, including DeepSWE and SWE-Marathon, in third-party runs, and publishes no numbers of its own. Meta's developer pages carry no prices or context windows.
good: Frontier coding and long-running agents — Meta's own positioning
Wonder Full tops third-party agentic runs, per Meta — no numbers published
limits: No prices, context windows or benchmark figures on Meta's developer pages — nothing to cite
The Muse CLI has a launch profile but no seat has run it, so the route is listed, not verified

families.name: Muse Spark
families.tagline: Meta's mid line — and its open-weight release.
families.summary: Muse Spark is the middle of Meta's lineup, with Muse Spark Open (816B) as the open-weight release — the most capable US open-weight model, in Meta's own words, served on SGLang, vLLM and Apple MLX. Meta publishes no prices or benchmarks for the Spark line.
good: Spark Open 816B: open weights, run it yourself on SGLang, vLLM or Apple MLX
The coding-optimized 1.2 is also served through OpenRouter
limits: No prices, context windows or dates published on Meta's developer pages
No TeamCLI route

families.name: Muse Glimmer
families.tagline: Meta's local, always-on agent model.
families.summary: Muse Glimmer is Meta's model for always-on local agents, available on Hugging Face. Meta's developer pages publish nothing else about it — no prices, no context window, no benchmarks.
good: Always-on local agents on your own hardware, on Hugging Face
limits: Nothing else published to cite
No TeamCLI route

claude-code.name: Claude Code
claude-code.reaches: Anthropic's own Claude models, run by Anthropic's CLI.
claude-code.account: An Anthropic subscription (Claude Pro or Max), or an Anthropic API key.
claude-code.login: Run the CLI once and sign in through the browser, or hand it an API key.
claude-code.profileNote: The model is read off Claude Code's own screen; the seat's label on team status comes from the file's display.

antigravity.name: Antigravity
antigravity.reaches: Gemini, Claude and GPT, through the Google AI Ultra pools.
antigravity.install: The desktop app, or the agy terminal client, from antigravity.google.
antigravity.account: A Google account on a Google AI plan (the Antigravity / Google AI Ultra pools).
antigravity.login: Sign in with the Google account the plan is on.
antigravity.profileNote: Antigravity replaced the hosted Gemini CLI for personal accounts; the model is set with the profile's own flag.

codex.name: Codex
codex.reaches: OpenAI's own GPT models, run by OpenAI's CLI.
codex.account: A ChatGPT plan, or an OpenAI API key.
codex.login: Run the CLI once and sign in with ChatGPT, or hand it an API key.
codex.profileNote: Codex updates itself, so the installed version moves on its own; the profile is tested against a known range.

cursor.name: Cursor
cursor.reaches: Claude, GPT, Gemini and Grok, on a Cursor plan.
cursor.install: Cursor, from cursor.com; the cursor-agent CLI ships with it.
cursor.profileNote: The seat declares the model it is for; the running model is chosen inside Cursor, which reads it off its own status row, and the seat's launch line carries no model flag.

grok.name: Grok CLI
grok.reaches: xAI's own Grok models, run by xAI's CLI.
grok.account: An xAI plan, or an API key.
grok.login: The first launch opens the browser to authenticate.
grok.profileNote: The running model is read off the composer's footer; a screen that shows none falls back to the launch line's model.

jules.name: Jules
jules.install: Nothing to install locally — Jules runs in the cloud; start at jules.google.com.
jules.account: A Google account (the Jules free tier or a paid plan).
jules.login: Sign in at jules.google.com with the Google account.
jules.profileNote: Jules picks its own Gemini model, so the seat sets model_from: launcher; its TUI has no auto-approve flag and herdr reads its pane unreliably, so the profile reads its session table by a screen module.

muse.name: Muse
muse.reaches: Meta's own Muse models, run by Meta's CLI.
muse.login: Sign in with the Meta account; it shows only inside the CLI's own /status.
muse.profileNote: Muse takes its rules as the seat's first message, and has no non-interactive login check in this version.

claude-code-endpoint.name: Claude Code with a provider endpoint
claude-code-endpoint.reaches: Any Anthropic-compatible endpoint — DeepSeek, Kimi and Z.ai GLM among them.
claude-code-endpoint.install: Install Claude Code, then a small launcher on the PATH that points it at the provider's base URL.
claude-code-endpoint.account: The provider's own API key, read from the OS keychain by the launcher — never from the team file.
claude-code-endpoint.login: Set the provider's API key where the launcher reads it; the launcher hands Claude Code the endpoint and the model.
claude-code-endpoint.profileNote: One line beside cli: claude-code — launch: my-lab-claude — is the whole difference; model_from: launcher says the launcher picks the model.

kimi.name: Kimi Code CLI
kimi.reaches: Moonshot's own Kimi models, run by Moonshot's CLI.
kimi.account: A Kimi Code membership, or a Kimi platform API key.
kimi.login: Run the CLI and use /login — an OAuth device flow, or a platform API key.
kimi.profileNote: Not a TeamCLI seat kind yet: there is no launch profile for the native Kimi CLI, so Kimi's models run here as Claude Code endpoint seats instead.

api.name: The API directly
api.reaches: The model over its vendor's API, without a CLI of its own.
api.login: Hold the vendor's API key. An Anthropic-compatible API runs here as a Claude Code endpoint seat; the others have no TeamCLI launch profile yet.
